originating_prompt:
One correction to your last Surzion turn, on the "Often ordered with" strips of the 22 surz_p_* product pages. You picked each strip's three products with a code range plus `neq` exclusions. That silently changes the set the day a product code is added inside a range. Page data-source filters now support the `in` operator (the engine already did; the page schema and designer now expose it):

  { "column": "PRODUCT_CODE", "op": "in", "value": { "source": "static", "value": "P001, P007, P012" } }

`value` is a comma-separated list; an empty list matches nothing. On every surz_p_* page replace the range + `neq` filters of the "often ordered with" data source with ONE `in` filter naming exactly the three PRODUCT_CODEs that page shows today, and order the repeat so the three appear in today's order. Change nothing else on the pages. Delegate to the smart-page-designer, run the smart-page-reviewer, and spot-check at least five pages' sources against the live product master so each returns exactly its three products. Delete your helper `.twasta/agent-work/apply_rel.py` if it is no longer needed.

Also, for your note on the "Applying as" strip: `{{me.signedIn}}` resolves to the string 'false' for a signed-out visitor, which the visibility condition treats as hidden — keep the condition as it is.

List what you changed and the spot-check results.
